basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 8.' and it opens '(Vers. 8.) Et mortua est Debbora nutrix Rebeccae, et sepulta est juxta Bethel. Si mortua'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 8.) Et mortua est Debbora nutrix Rebeccae, et sepulta est juxta Bethel. Si mortua est nutrix Rebeccae nomine Debbora, ut Septuaginta quoque hic Interpretes transtulerunt, et ipsum verbum est Hebraicum (מינקת) MENECETH: scire non possumus, quare ibi substantiam posuerunt, hic nutricem.
